annotation.title_clean: Statement of Max Fenkell, Scale AI, before the House Committee on Homeland Security Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection: DeepSeek and Unitree Robotics: Examining the National Security Risks of PRC Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Autonomous Technologies and Building a Secure U.S. Technology Base
annotation.title_en: Statement of Max Fenkell, Scale AI, before the House Committee on Homeland Security Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection: DeepSeek and Unitree Robotics: Examining the National Security Risks of PRC Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Autonomous Technologies and Building a Secure U.S. Technology Base
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Scale AI (Max Fenkell); U.S. House Committee on Homeland Security hearing materials
annotation.venue: U.S. House Committee on Homeland Security, Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection hearing
annotation.summary_en: Congressional hearing statement by Scale AI arguing China dominates robotics AI data and deployment, creating national security risks. It urges investigating Chinese robotics data as a threat, treating US data as a strategic asset, and boosting US investment. The hearing materials also address security risks of PRC robots such as Unitree and LiDAR sensors.
key_provisions_or_claims: China holds roughly 90% of commercially available robotics AI data and produces it at 60% lower cost, per Scale's estimates.
Reliance on Chinese data creates supply chain, data poisoning and backdoor risks.
Congress should investigate Chinese robotics data as a national security threat and treat US data as a national asset.
Four actions are needed to win on data and implementation.
Chinese LiDAR and robots in critical infrastructure pose spatial-data and espionage risks.
